name: discs_nil
note: json.Marshal of a nil map[int]string is `null` (album_repository.go:90 json.Marshal(a.Album.Discs))

name: discs_empty_non_nil
note: json.Marshal of a non-nil empty map is {}

name: discs_integer_keys_string_order
note: KEY ORDER CONTRACT: Go sorts integer map keys AS STRINGS — 1, 10, 2 (not numeric 1, 2, 10). Next key 100 sorts between 10 and 2.

name: discs_i64_and_negative_keys
note: Go int is 64-bit on the target: keys beyond i32 and negative keys are valid; encoding/json sorts their decimal strings lexicographically.

name: discs_single
note: single key

name: discs_escaping_unicode
note: values with < > & and U+2028/U+2029 — Go's json.Marshal escapes them; serde_json does not (settled divergence: shape + round-trip, not bytes)

name: folder_ids_nil
note: json.Marshal of a nil []string is `null` (album_repository.go:86 json.Marshal(a.Album.FolderIDs))

name: folder_ids_empty_non_nil
note: json.Marshal of a non-nil empty []string is []

name: folder_ids_values
note: element order is preserved (slices keep input order)

name: folder_ids_escaping
note: < > & and U+2028/U+2029 in list elements

name: image_files_nil_write
note: folder_repository.go:48-50: ImageFiles == nil -> the LITERAL "[]" arm, never json.Marshal(nil) (which would be null). The harness executes the exact PostMapArgs expression.

name: image_files_empty_non_nil_write
note: a non-nil empty []string takes the json.Marshal arm and yields [] anyway — both arms agree on [] for empty

name: image_files_values_write
note: non-nil image files: the json.Marshal arm, element order preserved, escaping per Go

name: read_discs_ok_string_order
note: json.Unmarshal into map[int]string succeeds; Go's marshal order of the result is the string-sorted key order

name: read_discs_i64_boundary
note: map[int]string accepts keys beyond i32 on the 64-bit Go target.

name: read_discs_negative_key
note: negative integer keys are valid and string-sort before positive keys.

name: read_discs_alias_keys_last_wins
note: alternate decimal spellings parse to the same int key; the later object member wins.

name: read_discs_fractional_key
note: a fractional object key is not an integer and must error.

name: read_discs_null
note: json.Unmarshal of `null` into map[int]string: no error, map left nil (PostScan guard a.Discs != "" skips this for the empty string, but null is a legal column value)

name: read_discs_empty_string
note: json.Unmarshal of the empty string into map[int]string errors (unexpected end of JSON input) — this is why the PostScan hook guards a.Discs != ""

name: read_discs_non_integer_key
note: a non-integer object key is a hard error into map[int]string

name: read_discs_non_integer_key_mixed
note: a non-integer key among valid ones is still a hard error

name: read_discs_non_string_value
note: a non-string value is a hard error into map[int]string

name: read_discs_null_value
note: a null value decodes to the zero value `""` with no error (Go behaviour pinned in the golden)

name: read_discs_wrong_type_array
note: a JSON array is a hard error into map[int]string

name: read_discs_empty_object
note: an empty object yields an empty (non-nil) map, no error

name: read_list_ok
note: json.Unmarshal into []string keeps element order

name: read_list_null
note: json.Unmarshal of `null` into []string: no error, slice left nil (nil-vs-empty IS representable on the read side)

name: read_list_empty_string
note: json.Unmarshal of the empty string into []string errors (unexpected end of JSON input) — why the folder hook guards ImageFiles != ""

name: read_list_empty_array
note: an empty array yields an empty (non-nil) slice, no error — distinct from null

name: read_list_non_string_element
note: a non-string element is a hard error into []string

name: read_list_null_element
note: a null element decodes to the zero value `""` with no error (Go behaviour pinned in the golden)

name: read_list_wrong_type_object
note: a JSON object is a hard error into []string
